answer: Each identity posts a 50-credit bond in the marble registry. Auditors in canyon-separated panels with no shared members check its work history against every prior identity and log the result. The audit fee for the k-th identity is 10+2(k-1) credits, as the search grows: the 1000th fake pays 2008 in fees plus 50 bond, and 1000 fakes pay 1,009,000 in fees plus 50,000 locked. An honest agent pays 50 once, refundable on clean exit, plus one 10 fee. A rented-audit ring fails when an umber panel from another canyon samples approved identities and slashes any panel that approved a duplicate.
